text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel is weak evidence on its own. Structural engineering is heavily male, so a four-man panel is roughly what chance would produce — it's consistent with bias but also with the sector's demographics. Leading with it makes you look like you're inferring discrimination from headcount, which is easy to dismiss.

Your stronger facts are substantive: nearly double the experience, a comparable licence, three major projects led, and a winning candidate whose stated edge is an unmeasured, subjective criterion. Plus two weeks of silence on a reasonable request for written reasons.

Chase the written explanation in writing, with a deadline. Ask what the scoring criteria and weightings were. Panel composition becomes relevant context only once you see those answers.
